rationale: A wins because it gives the founder more usable routes without losing discipline: "How to get Patagonia gear repaired for free now that it's in every store" is a real service-journalism lane, not padding. B is tighter and smart, especially "The retailer that won't say how much money its sustainability story makes," but it sends the next move toward "newsjack-detector" when the company already has a live launch peg. That is over-clever machinery where a fit-checked beat list would do the job.
gaps_in_A: "How to get Patagonia gear repaired for free now that it's in every store" overpromises. Only basic repairs are free; complex repairs are charged at cost.
"Patagonia expands a program built to sell you less clothing" is sharp, but it is still an inference. The update does not prove repair reduces new purchases.
"no new apparel line announced" is thin evidence for strategic restraint. A correctly flags this later, but the angle leans on it too hard.
"whether repair-and-resale is graduating from boutique perk to standard retail infrastructure" needs outside comparison before it can stand as a trend claim.
gaps_in_B: "free repairs at every US store" is too broad. The supplied fact is free basic repairs, with complex repairs charged at cost.
"the repair and resale programs are being expanded as described" smuggles in a resale expansion. The update gives a resale milestone, not a new resale rollout.
"Next step: newsjack-detector" is the wrong first move for a launch announcement with its own why-now. Pick the beat and build a fit-checked journalist list.
B misses the consumer-service angle entirely: drop-off, mail-in, free-versus-at-cost, and turnaround are a clean reader-facing story.
